    Website is what the website's rate card charges for the order's size; Charged is the freight on the invoices; Cost is what the carriers charged us; Gap is Charged minus Cost. Matched by customer name across the three reports ("3 of 3" in column F): . A customer with several orders in the period counts as one row, with their charges and shipments added together. "Cost us" uses the invoiced cost where the carrier has billed it and the carrier's estimate where it hasn't yet (the match file's own summary counts unbilled shipments as $0), plus 10% GST. "We charged" is the freight charged on the invoices. Click an order to find it on the map. Customer names, emails and phone numbers are not included.

    What a customer pays

    Delivering toFromMetroOuter metroRegional

    Prices include GST and are per order, as set in each state's tab of the shipping sheet ("Freight Charges for … Orders"). The destination tab follows the website's postcode list, so a few border towns use the neighbouring state's tab (Queanbeyan uses ACT, Tweed Heads uses QLD, Wentworth uses VIC). "First choice" is the warehouse at the top of the sheet's Source Hierarchy preference list for that state. Click a postcode for every size, both services and delivery times.

    Postcodes by state

    StatePostcodesMetroOuter metroRegionalRemote (ABS)

    Australia Post zones come from Australia Post's MyPost Business postcode list: Metro = Capital City (the eight capitals), Outer metro = Major Areas (e.g. Gold Coast, Newcastle, Geelong, Launceston), Regional = Rural (each state's "Outer" postcodes), plus Remote Islands & Locations. Australia Post notes that TAS Other postcodes don't get Zone 1 pricing. Postcode locations and remoteness (ABS Remoteness Areas 2021) come from the Australian Postcodes dataset; each dot sits at the average position of the postcode's suburbs, PO-box and business-only postcodes (rings) are placed at their post office. Remote islands and the Antarctic postcode are drawn in dashed boxes at the map's edge, out of their true position. Australia Post's ranges also include about 800 numbers that aren't real postcodes; those can't be shown. State outlines are simplified from Natural Earth via world-geojson. The ACT sits inside the NSW outline. Warehouses are placed at their suburb's centre, and "postcodes" beside each one counts the postcodes it is closest to in a straight line (road distance will differ).
